items.title: A map whose fibers are contractible can be made into a half adjoint equivalence

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 447-449 (book Theorem 4.4.3): for every map f, contractibility of its fibers implies that it is a half adjoint equivalence. The statement is an implication between two structures and the proof (source lines 450-458) has to construct each piece of the target structure from the hypothesis: the inverse map is the first component of a center of contraction, the homotopy is the witness that this point lies in the fiber, and the coherence datum, which is where the real work is, is first reduced through the cited lemma to a path inside a fiber and then produced explicitly from the contraction of that fiber as a concatenation of the two contraction paths. The reduction of the coherence to a path in a fiber, and the choice of its two endpoints, are invisible in the statement.
